sources.content: Proposal MB-112: column-level lineage in Mallowby. Mallowby, our data pipeline platform, records lineage today only at the table level, so when a source column changes, owners cannot tell which downstream dashboards use it. In the last quarter, 11 incidents came from renamed or dropped columns. The change: parse every SQL transform at deploy time and store, for each output column, the input columns it reads. Lineage is stored in a new table, `lineage_columns`, in the metadata database.

Scope and limits. Version 1 covers SQL transforms only; Python transforms keep table-level lineage. Queries that use `SELECT *` are expanded using the schema at deploy time. Parsing may add at most 2 seconds to a deploy; transforms that take longer are marked as partial and skipped. The lineage view in the web console shows at most 3 levels upstream and downstream by default. Rollout: an internal beta in January 2027 for the analytics team, then general availability once parse failures stay under 1 percent for a month.

claims.text: Mallowby version 1 column lineage covers SQL transforms only.

Mallowby stores column lineage in a table named lineage_columns.
